AND WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL. A command line that has to be remembered is a command line that
gets typed wrong, and the way it gets typed wrong here is pointing a committed run at the
wrong roster. `--fleet` refuses that outright; this file means nobody has to type it.
//fleet: The roster the broker must be holding. DUM checks and REFUSES on a mismatch rather than
warning — the caller of a committed run is a loop, and nobody reads a loop's warnings.
It is not a filter: with no --agent scope DUM drives every character that broker holds.
//control: The broker's loopback RPC. Default http://127.0.0.1:8901.
//log_dir: Where a committed run writes its log, relative to the repository root. Default `var`.
A bot whose log went to the terminal that started it has no log the moment that terminal
closes; the harness paid for that lesson with a broker whose whole ancestry was dead and
whose output was going to a temp directory that gets cleaned up.
Use --log <path> for a one-off, or --no-log to print only.
//courier_requests: The spell-training plan (a shift station with plan: spell-training) asks the courier for
reagents by writing its trainers' lines into the harness's courier request file, and costs
each drill from the harness's kod spell catalogue. Both are paths on this machine, so they
live here and never in a doctrine. Relative paths are read from the repository root.
Leave them out and the plan still places and buffs, but writes no requests and drills nothing.
//supervisor_state_dir: Where supervisor heartbeats, stop files and logs live. Default var/supervisors. Every
supervisor a doctrine declares writes <dir>/<id>.supervisor.json; see docs/supervisors.md.
